Resolves #22032

Top-labelled text fields now give a Grid row enough height for both the label and the input. Counter and in-flow error layouts retain their content-sized grid.

Evidence: L3 (compiled CSS and real fields in headless Chromium) → L3 required (AC-1 through AC-3).

CI jobs: +0.

## AC Evidence

| Criterion | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| AC-1 | The new component case mounts two real text fields in an Engine Grid layout. On the original stylesheet the first input ended at Y 52 px with its field ending at Y 32 px. The fixed field contains its input and leaves space before the next label. |
| AC-2 | The Text, TextArea, ComboBox and Select component specs passed locally, including the existing top-label, counter and in-flow error cases. The checkout flex control retained its 46 px field and 9 px gap. |
| AC-3 | In the controlled checkout Grid, both Neo Light and Neo Dark moved from 27 to 46 px per top-labelled field. The input wrapper fits the field and the next label has 13 px of clearance. |

## Deltas from ticket

The fix is a low-specificity height rule before the existing counter and validation sizing. The regression uses the normal Engine Grid layout and TextField factory.

## Test Evidence

Chromium reproduced the 6 px input-to-label overlap in the real checkout fields with the shipping group placed in single-column Grid at 1440 × 900. The component regression went red before the CSS change and green after it. All 42 targeted component tests passed.

| Before | With the fix |
| --- | --- |
| ![Checkout input overlaps the next label in Grid](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/c12f95569f5afe0970e0470e99febe5f60611853/review-evidence/22032/grid-before.jpg?raw=true) | ![Each checkout input and label fits in its Grid row](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/c12f95569f5afe0970e0470e99febe5f60611853/review-evidence/22032/grid-after.jpg?raw=true) |

Frame critique: The taller shipping fieldset shifts the centered form card upward. Every label and input now has room inside its own row.

### `@neo-opus-grace` (APPROVED) reviewed on 2026-11-22T22:42:21Z

# PR Micro-Review

**Class:** micro — a five-line CSS height rule plus one component case. It fixes one selector's sizing and teaches no architectural concept.

**Verdict:** Approved

**Glance:** A top-labelled `Text` field inherits the single-line `height` of `.neo-textfield`. In a Grid row nothing rescues it (a flex column's `min-height: auto` does), so its input spills below the field onto the next label. Verified at `18af1e6807`. `&:where(.label-top) { height: auto; }` has the base rule's specificity (0,1,0) and comes after its `height`, so it wins there. The in-flow error rule (`:where(:has(…))`, also 0,1,0) comes later and keeps `max-content`, and `.neo-has-character-count` (0,2,0) wins outright, which is the order #22032 asks for. No later `.label-top` rule sets a height; the block further down only sets direction and margins. CI's components shard 2/3 ran the new Grid case green. The before/after frames show the overlap gone and the flex Payment fieldset unchanged. What I looked for and did not find: a layout that depended on the old fixed height. In a flex column `min-height: auto` already gave 46 px (AC-2), and in a horizontal row the field now takes its content height instead of overflowing, which is the same fix. The diff touches only the named rule and its spec.

**Findings:** None.
